Oracle Java Language Specification 26 primary-source snapshot

claims.text: The preserved source asks for handwritten DCL singleton code, why volatile is needed, and the principle.

A volatile write happens-before each subsequent volatile read of the same field, and monitor unlock happens-before subsequent lock; these JLS rules support the candidate safe-publication and mutual-exclusion explanation.
The exact candidate compiles and independently validates private static volatile publication, private construction and stable identity under concurrent access.

findings: The source boundary exactly asks for handwritten double-check singleton code, why volatile is needed, and the underlying principle.

The answer separates initialization mutual exclusion from safe publication: synchronized protects the compound creation path while volatile connects the lock-free fast-path read to the publishing write.
Oracle JLS 26 section 17.4.5 was checked source-first and states the volatile write-to-subsequent-read and monitor unlock-to-subsequent-lock happens-before rules used by the explanation.
Oracle JLS 26 section 8.3.1.4 was checked source-first for volatile field semantics; the answer avoids relying on an implementation-only main-memory slogan.
The exact candidate compiles under Java 21, has a private static volatile instance and private constructor, and an independent 192-thread stress harness observes one stable identity.
The answer explicitly notes that volatile does not make the compound null-check/construction atomic and that reflection/serialization guarantees are separate concerns.
No fabricated production experience is claimed.
